Recent research supports separating observed feedback from inferred intent. [Herlihy et al. (2024)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v244/herlihy24a.html) show that recommendation chatbots can make inappropriate assumptions under underspecified requests. [From Feedback to Checklists (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17717), in clinical documentation, demonstrates how actual user feedback can yield structured, interpretable evaluation criteria; transfer to recommendation remains a hypothesis. Recommendation-specific evidence also cautions against evaluator priming: [Spotify’s 2026 study](https://research.atspotify.com/publications/intent-description-anchoring-bias-in-llm-as-a-judge-evaluation-of-recommendation-systems) found that algorithm descriptions changed judgments of identical recommendation lists. Hide model identities and optimization claims from annotators.

A proposed annotation scheme for the twenty training users should separate immediate choice, explicitly deferred interest, functional redundancy, compatibility concern, and unidentified content. Treat these as potentially overlapping labels, each requiring a feedback excerpt or identifiable evidence from titles, descriptions, timestamps, or histories. Historical interaction alone establishes neither ownership nor redundancy; missing specifications establish compatibility uncertainty, not incompatibility. No selection does not establish dislike or deferred interest. Preserve unknown/insufficient-evidence labels and avoid inferring latent traits.

Assess annotation quality through independent double annotation, per-label agreement, Cohen’s κ or Krippendorff’s α, disagreement review, and abstention coverage. Report denominators and retain original judgments before adjudication. Evidence extraction needs semantic checking: a [2026 evidence-requirement study](https://www.cureus.com/articles/493345-show-your-work-verbatim-evidence-requirements-and-automated-assessment-of-large-language-models-for-biomedical-text-processing-of-trial-eligibility-criteria) found that mechanically valid quotations did not reliably support assigned labels. These annotations can diagnose why related recommendations fail; they do not establish improvements in benchmark HR@10.
